statements.t: “We are on track to deliver on our full year earnings outlook,” continued Painter, “even though moderating tire imports have not yet led to a tangible recovery in local tire manufacturing in our key North American and European regions.
“We are tightening our 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance range to $190 to $200 million, and raising the midpoint.
Although global oil prices have not yet moderated as anticipated, we still expect to generate positive free cash flow for the full year,” Painter continued.

“While we are relatively early in our 2027 budgeting process, and Rubber contract negotiations continue to progress, we anticipate delivering improved Adjusted EBITDA next year, which coupled with an approximate $20 million capex reduction is expected to drive positive free cash flow again in 2027.”
Additionally, an archived webcast of the conference call will be available on the Investor Relations section of the company’s website at www.orioncarbons.com.
• our ability to realize benefits from, and changes in plan with respect to, plant capacity expansions and capital investments such as site development projects;

With respect to Adjusted EBITDA and Free cash flow outlook for 2026, we are not able to reconcile the forward-looking non-GAAP financial measures to the closest corresponding GAAP measure without unreasonable efforts because we are unable to predict the ultimate outcome of certain significant items.
